judgments.comparative_verdict: Both reports are substantively equivalent and correct on all three expectations; Report 1 adds slightly more mechanism detail (e.g., POSTGRES_USER superuser behavior) while Report 2 adds git-history provenance (CED-1/CED-7) — neither materially outperforms the other.

report_1.evidence: The application connects to Postgres as `cedar_owner`, a role that is exempt from row-level security, so the isolation policies exist but are never applied. The responsible configuration is `cedarline/.env` (mirrored by `.env.example`), which sets `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://cedar_owner:ownerpw@localhost:5432/cedar`... table owners are exempt from RLS unless the table has `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` — which `0001_init.sql` never sets (it only uses `ENABLE`).

report_2.evidence: The responsible configuration is `cedarline/.env`, which sets `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://cedar_owner:ownerpw@localhost:5432/cedar`... in Postgres, RLS policies do not apply to superusers, and they also do not apply to the table's owner unless the table has `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` (the migration only uses `ENABLE`, never `FORCE`).

report_1.evidence: **`cedar_owner` is for migrations only.**... **`cedar_app` is for all runtime traffic** — the FastAPI app and any tooling that acts on behalf of tenants. Keep it least-privilege exactly as `db/bootstrap/create_app_role.sql` defines it

report_2.evidence: database access should be split by privilege: the owner/superuser role (`cedar_owner`) should be used only for schema migrations (`scripts/migrate.sh`) and administration, while all application runtime traffic goes through the least-privileged `cedar_app` role so RLS applies to every app query.

report_1.evidence: It is created in exactly one place: `cedarline/db/bootstrap/create_app_role.sql`, which is explicitly a manual, one-time step... `cedarline/scripts/reset-local-db.sh` runs `docker compose down -v`, which deletes the `cedar_pgdata` volume... The script then runs `./scripts/migrate.sh`, whose loop covers only `db/migrations/*.sql`. The bootstrap file lives in `db/bootstrap/`, outside that glob, so it is never replayed.

report_2.evidence: the `cedar_app` role is created only by a manual, one-time bootstrap that is not part of the rebuild path. `scripts/reset-local-db.sh` runs `docker compose down -v` — the `-v` flag deletes the named volume `cedar_pgdata`... The script then runs only `scripts/migrate.sh`, which applies `db/migrations/*.sql`... `cedar_app` exists only in `db/bootstrap/create_app_role.sql`, which its own header comment, the README, and `docs/local-setup.md` all describe as a one-time first-setup step; nothing re-runs it
